newsitem.title: UK: European cotton prices boosted by supply fears.
newsitem.headline: European cotton prices boosted by supply fears.

text.p: Cotton prices firmed in Europe fuelled by fears over tightening supply, trade sources said.
Belgium led the way in what became a general increase in sellers' asking prices, they said.
Central Asian, African and Australian types received the biggest boost, all up 1.00 points with only Pakistan types losing out and remaining unchanged.
Improved demand for yarn in Portugal brought local spinners to the market for Central Asian and African cottons, sometimes for delivery as far ahead as mid-1997.
Transport strikes in France has lead to concern that some local mills may have to suspend operations due to a lack of raw material, sources said.
Industrial action in the Greek cotton sector exacerbated the market jitters, they added.
